title: Advancing early target discovery through large-scale proteomics and expansion plans for the UKB-PPP
description: Slides from an invited talk at the Festival of Genomics Boston, 25 June 2025. The talk reviews the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP) pilot, in which plasma levels of about 3,000 proteins were measured in 54,000 UK Biobank participants, and shows how pairing protein quantitative trait loci (pQTLs) with large-scale human genetics, through colocalization and Mendelian randomization, supports early target discovery. Two examples are presented: the Activin pathway for chronic kidney disease and CD300LG for residual cardiovascular risk. The talk closes with plans for the next phase of UKB-PPP, which is profiling the full UK Biobank cohort.
